comment: Live proof for the double-close fix (PR 4/4 of 'close nested node boundaries on failure'): an edge-wired `subgraph` node (`inner_sub`) nested one level inside another edge-wired `subgraph` node (`outer`), whose own inner node raises. Two DISTINCT start/end pairs must balance for node_id `inner_sub`: the run loop's own (path `outer>inner_sub`) and `SubGraphNode`'s self-emitted inner boundary (path `outer>inner_sub>inner_sub`, #313). An earlier version of this fix skipped the loop-level close whenever node_type==subgraph, reasoning it would double the self-close — it actually left the loop-level start permanently dangling, since the two pairs are at different paths, not duplicates.
